credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Bertram Dobell (1842–1914) was an English bookseller and literary scholar. A largely self-taught man, he published or reissued works by writers including James Thomson and Thomas Traherne, and wrote poetry, criticism and biography himself.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Microcosm
poems.author: Bertram Dobell
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
His home a speck in a vast Universe,
He a mere atom on that tiny speck,
Victim of countless evils that coerce
And force him onward on a pathless track:
And yet a being made to dominate
O'er all things else by mind's controlling power:
Spoilt favourite at once and sport of fate,
Football of fortune, time's consummate flower!

To him alone did Nature's self impart
A spark of her divinest energy,
With power to create a world of Art,
And intellect to solve all mystery:
So great arid yet so little! blest and curst —
Nature's most noble offspring — yet her worst!
